correctness.rationale: The exact coding is reconstructed by telescoping the established monotone semiconjugacy. At depth \(n\) the \(n+1\) nonempty Sturmian cylinders have Euclidean diameter at most \(\lambda^n/(1-\lambda)\), while distinct cylinders are separated by at least \(\lambda^{n-1}(1-2\lambda)/(1-\lambda)\), strictly larger when \(\lambda<1/3\). Continued-fraction convergents for bounded-type rotation numbers bound each coding arc by \(O(1/n)\), supplying a probability mass bound \(C/\log(e/r)\) and hence a positive critical gauge; the finite upper gauge follows from the cylinder covering. Finite tests give consistency only, not an infinite proof.
